tools.name: remind_me
tools.description: Sign the user up for an email reminder before a public event that search_events returned, or for an email when a value beep.me reads crosses a line the user chose (a watch from search_events). Ask the user for their email address first (never guess it) and pass either the event id, or the watch's so

tools.description: Switch the user's beep.me reminders on with the 6-digit code from beep.me's confirmation email, so they don't have to leave the chat to click its link. Only with a code the user has typed into the chat themselves: never guess one, never reuse a code from earlier. Pass the address the reminder was ma

tools.name: my_reminders
tools.description: List the reminders on the signed-in user's beep.me account: each upcoming event with when its email arrives, and each team they follow. Use it when the user asks what beep.me reminds them about, and before stop_reminder to find the id. Needs the user signed in to beep.me.

tools.name: stop_reminder
tools.description: Stop one reminder on the signed-in user's beep.me account: an event by its event_id, or every match of a followed team by its follow_id, both from my_reminders. Only when the user asked to stop it. Needs the user signed in to beep.me.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: my_reminders · Private data: search_events · Public sink: remind_me, follow_team, confirm_email, my_reminders.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: my_reminders · Private data: search_events · Public sink: remind_me, follow_team, confirm_email, my_reminders

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search_events" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
